Below is a single, consolidated 12‑week programme you can give the client. It starts 2026‑06‑01 and integrates strength, plyometrics, a controlled HIIT‑style metabolic day, progressive aerobic base work, an anti‑inflammatory nutrition plan, and symptom‑aware rules for flow and flare windows. I’ve respected the restrictions you gave: on flow days AND flare days — no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping. I’ve marked when to avoid higher intensity and which sessions convert to conservative alternatives. If you want a dated printable calendar I can map each session to exact dates and move sessions to client availability.

Quick reference — dates & restrictions
- Cycle: last period began 2026‑05‑04; 27‑day cycle; flow lasts ~4 days.
  - Predicted flow windows during this 12‑week programme:
    - 2026‑05‑31 → 2026‑06‑03 (covers start week)
    - 2026‑06‑27 → 2026‑06‑30
    - 2026‑07‑24 → 2026‑07‑27
    - 2026‑08‑20 → 2026‑08‑23
  - Flare windows you gave: 2026‑07‑10 → 2026‑07‑13 and 2026‑08‑04 → 2026‑08‑07.
- Rule: on any day that falls within a flow window OR a flare window, do NOT perform: HIIT, heavy Valsalva (no maximal singles or encouraged breath‑holding), or jumping/plyometrics. Replace higher‑intensity sessions with conservative alternatives (light resistance, mobility, pool walking, steady low‑impact cardio).

Overall weekly structure (typical non‑flow week)
- 4 main sessions per week: 2 heavy strength days (lower/upper), 1 full‑body/conditioning or metabolic day (includes HIIT‑style on non‑flow days), 1 plyometric/skill or long steady cardio day — plus 1–2 optional recovery/mobility short sessions.
- Cardio frequency increases across phases from 2→3→3–4 sessions/week with one long steady session weekly.
- On flow/flare days: sessions become low‑load, higher‑rep (12–20), mobility, or pool walking. No HIIT or plyo.

Phases overview
- Phase 1: Foundation & symptom‑aware conditioning — Weeks 1–4 (2026‑06‑01 → 2026‑06‑28)
  - Aim: movement quality, diaphragmatic breathing, build aerobic base, light–moderate loads.
- Phase 2: Intensified strength & aerobic build (includes HIIT & plyo introduction) — Weeks 5–8 (2026‑06‑29 → 2026‑07‑26)
  - Aim: increase load on main lifts (5×5 and heavier 4–6 rep work), introduce one controlled low‑impact HIIT metabolic day and low‑impact plyometrics (only on non‑flow/non‑flare days).
  - Note: Flare 2026‑07‑10→13 — convert those days to conservative work.
- Phase 3: Consolidation, higher aerobics, plyo progression & test planning (no true 1RM) — Weeks 9–12 (2026‑07‑27 → 2026‑08‑23)
  - Aim: consolidate strength, longer zone‑2 sessions, advanced plyo if tolerated, deload in Week 12. End‑of‑phase testing to be submaximal (3–5RM) to estimate 1RM only.

Daily session format (typical strength session)
- Warm‑up (8–12 min): light cardio, diaphragmatic breathing, dynamic mobility, activation (glute bridges, band walks, scapular sets).
- Main strength work (30–40 min): compounds then accessories; breathe diaphragmatically, exhale on concentric, avoid breath‑holding.
- Conditioning / cardio (optional finisher 10–20 min) if scheduled that day and not on a flow/flare day.
- Cooldown (5–8 min): breathing, pelvic‑floor focused stretches, light mobility.

Progression & monitoring
- Increase load when client completes top end of rep range at RPE ≤7–8 with good form. Use RPE and symptoms to modify.
- Keep a log of RPE, pelvic pain (0–10), menstrual phase, and session notes. If pelvic pain increases >3–4/10 or trends upward, reduce intensity and consult clinician/physio.
- Submaximal testing (3–5RM) at end of Phase 3 only if symptom-free and on non‑flow/non‑flare day; true 1RM testing is not recommended.

Nutrition (anti‑inflammatory) — summary
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day (higher on training days). Emphasise whole food sources.
- Prioritise: omega‑3 rich fish, leafy greens, berries, whole grains, legumes, nuts/seeds, extra virgin olive oil, turmeric/ginger, fermented foods (if tolerated).
- Limit: processed foods, trans fats, excess red meat, excessive caffeine/alcohol, refined sugars.
- Supplements to discuss with clinician: omega‑3 (EPA/DHA), vitamin D (if deficient), magnesium, curcumin.
- Meal timing: small carb+protein snack pre/post training. On flow/flare days favour warm, smaller frequent meals if appetite reduced.
- Keep a food + symptom diary for 2–4 weeks to identify triggers.

Full 12‑week week‑by‑week summary
(Each week below lists the four main sessions and cardio notes, with instructions for flow/flare day swaps where applicable. Swap days to client schedule as needed; ensure plyo/HIIT never falls on a flow/flare day.)

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation & Build (June 1 → June 28)
Week 1 (2026‑06‑01 → 06‑07) — Predicted flow 31 May → 3 Jun (conservative early)
- Session 1 (Lower focus): Goblet squats 3×10; RDL DB 3×10; Stationary split squat 3×8/side; Clamshells 3×12; Bird‑dog 3×8/side. Low‑impact 10–12 min bike finisher optional. On flow days: reduce load to bodyweight, 12–20 reps, focus on breathing & mobility.
- Session 2 (Upper + core): Incline push‑up/DB press 3×8–10; One‑arm DB row 3×10; Seated DB press 3×10; Banded face pull 3×15; Dead bug 3×10/side. Farmer carry 3×40–60 s.

- Session 4 (Full‑body): Trap bar/dumbbell deadlift 3×8; Bulgarian split squat 3×8/side; Pull‑up progression 3×8–10; Single‑arm DB press 3×10; Pallof press 3×12/side.

- Session 2 Upper: Progress DB loads lightly; add 1 rep/set.

Short answer: No — I do not recommend 1RM testing at the end of Phase 3 for this client.

Why not
- 1RM testing requires near‑maximal single‑rep efforts that typically provoke heavy Valsalva (breath‑holding and very high intra‑abdominal pressure), which you specifically restricted for this client on flow and flare days and is inadvisable given pelvic pain/Stage III endometriosis.
- Max testing increases intra‑abdominal and pelvic pressure, which can exacerbate pelvic pain, provoke symptom flare, or irritate pelvic structures in people with moderate–severe endometriosis.
- It also increases risk of compensatory breathing, pelvic‑floor over‑coactivation or strain, and injury if form breaks down at heavy loads.

Safer alternatives (recommended)
- Estimated 1RM from multiple‑rep tests (submaximal testing)
  - Use a conservative 3–8 rep max (3RM–8RM) protocol on a non‑flow/non‑flare day with good recovery and then estimate 1RM with validated formulas (Epley, Brzycki). Example: if she can perform 5 reps with X kg at RPE ~8, estimate 1RM rather than pushing to a true single.
  - Advantages: much lower peak intra‑abdominal pressure, less neural strain, still gives a reliable estimate for programming.

- Repetition‑to‑failure testing at submaximal loads (RPE / reps in reserve)
  - Use a heavy working set to near failure (e.g., RPE 8–9) for 3–6 reps, then estimate 1RM. Coach breathing (exhale on concentric) and avoid breath‑holding.

- Velocity‑based or bar‑speed testing
  - If you have access to a linear position transducer or smartphone apps that estimate bar speed, use bar speed at submaximal loads to estimate 1RM. Low intra‑abdominal pressure because loads remain submaximal.

- Predicted 1RM using training logs
  - Use the heaviest load she handled for multiple reps across the cycle and apply an estimation formula. Track progress across phases.

- Only on a well‑recovered, non‑flow/non‑flare day (avoid within ~3 days prior to expected menses and outside flare windows).
- Medical clearance from her clinician confirming it is safe given her Stage III endometriosis and current symptoms.
- Very experienced spotters/coaching, gradual warm‑up protocol, and strict breathing coaching to avoid Valsalva (but note avoiding Valsalva makes true maximal expression harder and may invalidate the test).
- Avoid testing movements that provoke pelvic pressure — prefer trap‑bar deadlift over conventional deadlift for safer torso position if clinician agrees.
- Keep loads submaximal if any pelvic symptoms are present.

- Choose key lifts (e.g., trap‑bar deadlift, back/front squat, bench press).
- Perform 3–5 rep max (3RM–5RM) tests on a single day (non‑flow/non‑flare) after a full warm‑up:
  - Warm‑up sets: empty bar ×10, 50% working ×5, 70% ×3.
  - Work sets: ramp to weight that gives 3–5 reps with good form (stop at RPE 8–9).

Formulas (examples)
- Epley: 1RM ≈ weight × (1 + reps/30)
- Brzycki: 1RM ≈ weight / (1.0278 − 0.0278 × reps)
- These give reasonable estimates using 3–8 rep maxes.

How to interpret results for programming
- Use estimated 1RM to set training percentages (e.g., 70–85% for strength blocks). Because estimates have error, use conservative percentages (e.g., treat as ~95% of true 1RM for heavy loading) and monitor tolerance.
- Prioritise RPE and reps‑in‑reserve over strict %s due to symptom variability.

Final recommendation
- Do not do true 1RM testing. Use submaximal rep‑max tests (3–5RM), velocity measures, or estimated 1RM from training logs. Obtain medical clearance if maximal testing is insisted upon, and only proceed with strict supervision and on non‑flow/non‑flare days.
